nukaiserburg.name: Kaiserburg
nukaiserburg.slogan: Where every emperor came to stay, high above the red roofs.
nukaiserburg.line: The Sinwell Tower takes its name from Middle High German 'sinwell', meaning perfectly round; only it and the Imperial Chapel came through 1945 intact.

nuplonlein.name: Plönlein
nuplonlein.slogan: Two roads, two towers, one very photographed fork.
nuplonlein.line: On 31 March 1945 bombs destroyed about 275 of Rothenburg's houses; roughly 265 were rebuilt, which is why the old town still looks whole.

nuduererhaus.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
nuduererhaus.slogan: The painter's own address, steps from the castle hill.
nuduererhaus.line: Albrecht Dürer lived and worked in this house from 1509 until his death in 1528.

nurathausturm.name: Rothenburg Town Hall Tower
nurathausturm.slogan: Climb the narrow stairs for the best view of the Tauber roofs.
nurathausturm.line: The Gothic back of the town hall dates from 1250; the Renaissance front was begun in 1572.

nudinkelsbuehlmuenster.name: St. George's Minster, Dinkelsbühl
nudinkelsbuehlmuenster.slogan: A late Gothic hall of light inside an unbroken ring of walls.
nudinkelsbuehlmuenster.line: Dinkelsbühl is one of only four German towns, with Rothenburg, Nördlingen and Berching, whose city walls are completely intact.
